labels.label: defi:categorie_C
findings: ETT.tex:233 the objects of C are topological spaces, but its morphisms are only 'non-decreasing maps', with no continuity asked. Formalized as written (no continuity); the author may want 'continuous non-decreasing maps'.
questions: (a) Does 'non-decreasing' cover the chronological relation as well, i.e. x ≤ y ⇒ f x ≤ f y AND x ≪ y ⇒ f x ≪ f y? Taken: yes, both (CObj.Hom.map_le, map_lt). Consequence, measured: under this reading a weak morphism from the lightlike line (ℝ,≤,∅) is exactly a causal curve, and one from the timelike line is exactly a chronal curve (weakMorphism_lightlikeLine_iff, weakMorphism_timelikeLine_iff).
Are the morphisms of C required to be continuous? Taken: no, as written.

labels.label: def:category_topological_spacetimes

hypotheses.note: used by no lemma; carried only in the bundled Spacetime structure on which the Category instance lives

findings: ETT.tex:255 'an open map inducing a sheaf morphism': continuity is implicit (φ⁻¹U must be open for the component at U to exist). Carried as an explicit field, per DEC-10. Naturality of the sheaf morphism is automatic, since every component is a restriction of φ.

A strong morphism is a weak morphism (StrongMorphism.weakMorphism); both classes contain the identity and are closed under composition, so the strong morphisms form a category (instCategorySpacetime). Openness of φ is not used for any of this.

Library, not paper: Causal/Curves.lean's docstring says a causal curve 'is the weak morphism ... from the segment with the causality of the timelike line'. Under reading (a) that is the chronal curve; the causal curve is the weak morphism from the LIGHTLIKE line. Under the ≤-only reading the docstring is correct. Worth one sentence there once (a) is ruled.
questions: (a) as for defi:categorie_C: the 'non-decreasing' of φ|V^|U is read on both relations.
In a weak morphism, are the 'neighbourhoods' U of φ(x) and V of x open? Taken: open (≤_V is only defined for V open).

labels.label: ex:open_subset

hypotheses.paper: uniqueness (first sentence): the inclusion is a strong morphism
hypotheses.note: false as written; unique when the inclusion also reflects the relations (eq_restrict); the restriction is in any case the greatest such causality (le_restrict)

hypotheses.paper: uniqueness (second sentence): φ is a local isomorphism
hypotheses.note: fails without a gluing property (the witness timelikeLineTop is not causal, not absolutely minimal, not a sheaf); unique among absolutely minimal causalities (LocalIsomorphism.unique)
pullback_localIsomorphism; the definition of the pull-back only needs φ continuous

hypotheses.paper: N a topological spacetime (second countable, Hausdorff)
hypotheses.note: the paper never states it of N; not asked; false in general for the source of a local homeomorphism (line with two origins)

findings: ETT.tex:260 uniqueness is false as written: the diagonal causality (≤_V equality on V, ≪_V empty) also makes the inclusion of any open W a strong morphism, since a strong morphism only asks the relations of W to imply those of M (openSubset_not_unique, on the timelike line). What is true: the restriction is the GREATEST such causality, and the unique one for which the inclusion also reflects the relations (an isomorphism onto W). Suggested wording: 'a unique structure for which the inclusion is an isomorphism onto its image' or 'the largest structure for which ...'.

ETT.tex:262 uniqueness fails without a gluing property; among absolutely minimal causalities it holds (LocalIsomorphism.unique). Witness (localIsomorphism_not_unique): id : ℝ → ℝ is a local isomorphism to the timelike line both from the timelike line and from timelikeLineTop, which relates every pair of ℝ in ℝ itself. timelikeLineTop is a causality only because the library, like the paper's 'equivalently' form, has no gluing axiom: it is not causal (timelikeLineTop_not_isCausal), not absolutely minimal (timelikeLineTop_not_absolutelyMinimal), and not local in the sheaf sense. The paper's own use at ETT.tex:599 (X causally arc-connected, hence absolutely minimal) supplies the hypothesis under which uniqueness holds.

ETT.tex:262 'local isomorphism of topological spacetimes' needs N second countable and Hausdorff, and the paper says nothing about N: the line with two origins mapping to ℝ is a local homeomorphism from a non-Hausdorff space. The formalization asks nothing of N (the pull-back exists regardless), so N is a topological spacetime only if those hypotheses are added.

ETT.tex:262 existence holds for every local homeomorphism with no hypothesis on M (Causality.pullback, pullback_localIsomorphism): chains of relations read through φ in open sets on which φ is injective.
ETT.tex:262 'local isomorphism of topological spacetimes' is not defined in the paper.
questions: Which corrected uniqueness does the author intend in the first sentence: 'greatest', or 'the inclusion is an isomorphism onto W'? Both are proved.
Which corrected uniqueness in the second sentence: among absolutely minimal causalities (proved), or another class?

Reading taken of 'local isomorphism': φ a local homeomorphism, each point with an open neighbourhood V, φ injective on V, such that for every open V' ⊆ V and y, z ∈ V': y ≤_{V'} z ⇔ φ y ≤_{φ(V')} φ z, and likewise for ≪.

'Carries a structure' was stated with LocalCausality W (kb/0001); LocalCausality.inclusionStrong_iff proves that InclusionStrong is exactly StrongMorphism (L.toSubtype) C Subtype.val on the subspace ↥W, so nothing is lost.

labels.label: defi:fonction_temps
findings: Under DEC-10 a time function must be an OPEN map. The Geroch sketch ETT.tex:1272-1276 shows only that t^± = ±μ_±(J^±(x)) are continuous ('time functions (hence continuous)') and never argues that t^±, or T = log(-t^-/t^+), is open; nor, under the within-components reading (b), that [T x, T y] ⊆ U whenever x ≤_{T⁻¹U} y. The second point is automatic there, because Geroch assumes causal arc-connectedness (isTimeFunction_iff_order); the openness is a gap in (i)⇒(ii) of theo:geroch.
Notation: ETT.tex:267 calls the timelike line '(ℝ,≤,≤)' while ETT.tex:1029 calls the target of a time function '(ℝ,≤,<)'; the relations defined at l.267-268 are ≤ and <, so l.267 should read (ℝ,≤,<).
questions: (a) Does 'non-decreasing' cover ≪ ↦ <? Taken: yes. Then a time function satisfies x ≪_V y ⇒ T x < T y (IsTimeFunction.lt) and is increasing along chronal curves (strictMonoOn).

(b) Which causality does ℝ carry on a disconnected open U: the order restricted to U (orderLine), or the order within the components of U (the timelike line of ex:causalities_lines)? Taken: the timelike line (Causal/Lines.lean's timelikeLine, reused). The two readings agree on a causally arc-connected M (isTimeFunction_iff_order) and differ in general: id is a time function on orderLine in the restricted reading and not in the components reading (orderLine_id_not_isTimeFunction). In the restricted reading a time function is just a continuous open map with ≤_M ⇒ ≤ and ≪_M ⇒ < (isTimeFunctionOrder_iff).

kb_proposals: A structure field 'for every open U, a morphism from φ⁻¹U' is stated as '∀ U V, (V : Set M) = φ ⁻¹' U → …': no continuity proof inside the statement, and SetLike.coe_injective recovers V = preimageOpens hc U when needed.

Opens of a subspace ↥W: push forward with imageOpens V := ⟨Subtype.val '' V, W.isOpen.isOpenMap_subtype_val _ V.isOpen⟩; Subtype.image_preimage_coe does not fire against the SetLike coercion of ↥W, prove val '' (val ⁻¹' U) = U ∩ W by ext.
A CObj-valued def used as a category object should be an abbrev, or the carrier (C.toCObj U).carrier does not unfold to ↥U and point coercions fail.
A causality is not determined by its restrictions to a cover: to prove two causalities equal from local data, ask absolute minimality of one (then le_of_transGen after TransGen.mono).
notes: Module builds standalone (lake build CausalScaffold.Morphism: 1414 jobs, no Causal.* or mathlib rebuild), zero sorry, zero warning, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound only (checked by a temporary #print axioms file, since removed). Imports Causal.ArcConnected, Causal.Lines, Causal.Local and three mathlib modules (IsLocalHomeomorph, CategoryTheory.Category.Basic, Order.IntermediateValue). No label is marked: three rest on readings (a)/(b)/(c) awaiting the author's ruling, and ex:open_subset's uniqueness is false as written in both sentences (two counterexamples proved). Once (a) and (b) are ruled as taken here, defi:categorie_C, def:category_topological_spacetimes and defi:fonction_temps can be marked without any change to the proofs. Two subtypes appear in statements, both as bridges and disclosed: Causality.toCObj (an object of C is a space) and LocalCausality.toSubtype / inclusionStrong_iff (the library's LocalCausality form is the paper's strong morphism on ↥W). Curves.lean's docstring sentence on weak morphisms from the timelike line is off under reading (a); see the finding under def:category_topological_spacetimes. Audit round (2026-10-29): docstrings and SCOPE now disclose that timelikeLineTop is a gluing-free pathology; two lemmas added (timelikeLineTop_not_isCausal, timelikeLineTop_not_absolutelyMinimal); no existing declaration renamed or retyped (CausalScaffold.Pushout imports this module).
